author: kxfx
text:
Hello fellow classmates!

I've been training and trading live in silent for about a year using RTM method. It's great to see a lot of great guys coming to RTM! congratulation to Salivan and other great traders who's ranked up recently!

The reason I'm writing this post is mainly to ask a question to all of you who successful (and trading live account) with this RTM style and willing to share me some info. I wonder if you can tell me how's your winrate % and average RR return? After about year of live account practice, my result is as follow:

- average Winrate = 24% per month - average RewardRiskRatio = 6:1 - data from 100 latest trades - trading style: PO at clean DP around QM and nice history/long term SR. - management style: Close half at FTA, not moving SL to BE. - problem: Chicken mindset. Often close trade too early before reaching place where I would put my buy (if I'm shorting) ==> This translated into my low one digit RR.

My question is: is it normal to get low winrate trading RTM method? One of my friend is also getting low winrate like 18% per month (but he has better two digits RR than me). Is this normal?

I was trying to be the fund trader in the past, but I saw my winrate is damn low so I decided to not apply for now. It's too embarrassing to apply because I saw how Salivan is getting about 10-20R per trade, which is daaaaaaamn amazing! (great job, Salivan!) I'm far from the level and need more training. I just need some confirmation from you guys about the winrate part.

If you are not comfortable writing it publicly, can you kindly PM your result, I just need to confirm about the winrate part. Thanks you in advance and have a great day guys!!

(P.S. I jumped immediately to live account instead of Demoing. The reason is because I want to master/conquer my own demon as soon as possible. I don't want to get very good at Demo and then destroy myself in live account because of the uncontrolled demon inside me. I saw a lot of great demo traders who got MCed once they go live. I want to avoid this, so live account with minimum position is the way to go - at least for me.)

Sorry I cant upload a chart from work. Any thoughts would be appreciated. Thank you all

IMHO, In general Price moves from FL to FL, But specifically, to the pip, price moves from DP to DP. If the DP resides in between the limits of the FL/FTR, even it reacts to that DP, we see it as reacting to the FL (because it is in between the limits of the FL/FTR(upper bound and the lower bound). If the DP is below or above the limits of the FL/FTR, we see sometimes price can go/spike to that DP. Just my two cents.

Very good question BTW. I would like to know others' opinions also.

author: ViTaLDRuG
text:
Edge wrote: On a second point I see FTRs on traders and charts I review and its not really a FTR/FL because if you drill down to 1min you see the real FTR/FL. Or is it all relative to what TF is being analysed. To me the LTF Fl/FTR holds more significance and the HTF is not the FTR.

Exactly.. To find the true FTR/FL, we need to go to the smallest possible TF. I did that too. But later I realized I was making things complicated myself. Lets assume, you found a FTR/FL in tick chart/1MIN (say you have historic tick data) in the past. You will have to find the FL/FTRs once price breaks the current FL/FTR. The ones you find next will also be in the 1 min/tick chart. Searching all those FLs/FTRs made me really tired. After all, we loose the HTF picture, if we are going to find the true FL/FTR in LTF.

For example, Lets say you have found a nice FL in LTF, and you now see it is engulfed(BTW I am still researching if the DP needs to be engulfed or just the FL). So we can assume that the price is going to turn. You have also found a nice FL in HTF. But it has not being engulfed yet. Would you still think that price is going to turn? IMO, I would take the HTF FL into consideration. BTW don't take what I say as it is. These things are what I have seen so far. I am just presenting my observations.

dengaima wrote: Hello Ifmyante:D

I am back with another question =)

I noticed my explanations are not understandable therefore I went straight to draw a picture

it's just my personal preference as i feel IF's journal is too long already

Assuming that there is no HigherTF barrier to the left of CPPAZ, and price has already cut through all the CPPAZ, i'd only care about both edges (incl. the kinks) of the CPPAZ. Quoted from Ignored Level article: These barriers are;

- The break into or out of Compression (extremes of CP) - Highs and Lows (S/R) - Left shoulders (LS)

It is truly interesting when there is some HigherTF barrier to the left of CPPAZ we currently see. The barrier would then cause an FTR at mid-CP (which would become FL quite often) which can turn price before the whole CPPAZ is spent; or although CPPAZ is all cut through it will become an important ignored level, therefore a swap level (if that's what you're looking for). Another thought i have is: The Higher the time & range we mark the chart, the more and the wider spaces we can find in LTF. The Less high the time & range we mark the chart, the number of spaces we find in LTF become more but tighter, and sometimes "stacked/swapped/blurred" - this is what drives me mad lately and very often cause the fatal mistake of "trying to catch every turns", which then cause unnecessary/unconfirmed/stupid trades.

Looking forward to inputs from you all.
